quotes.text: This page describes usage recording for basic usage-based billing, where you send meter events to the Stripe `/v1/billing/meter_events` endpoint and Stripe aggregates them at the end of the billing period. If you’re evaluating a new integration, [Metronome](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/usage-based.md) handles event ingestion differently and is recommended for most new use cases.

In Metronome, you send usage events to Metronome’s ingest API rather than to Stripe directly. Metronome processes events in real time, applies your pricing configuration, and tracks running balances and usage totals continuously, so you and your customers can see current usage at any point during the billing period, not just at invoice time.

The Billing Meters approach on this page is appropriate only if you’re already using Billing Meters to bill customers today. For a new integration, including adding usage-based pricing to existing flat-rate subscriptions, use [Metronome](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/usage-based.md) instead of building custom event recording infrastructure.
Stripe processes meter events asynchronously, so aggregated usage in meter event summaries and on upcoming invoices might not immediately reflect recently received meter events.
[Use Amazon S3](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/recording-usage-in-bulk.md): Use Amazon S3 to add customer usage data in bulk.

old_evidence.text: Throughout each billing period, you must record usage in Stripe to bill your customers the correct amounts. You can decide how often you record usage in Stripe. You can record usage in Stripe using the Dashboard or API.
Stripe processes meter events asynchronously, so aggregated usage in meter event summaries and on upcoming invoices might not immediately reflect recently received meter events.
[Use the API](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/recording-usage-api.md): Use the Stripe API to record customer usage data.

findings: The 2026-11-07 same-URL capture adds a substantive recommendation: basic Stripe Billing Meters event recording is framed for existing Billing Meters users; Stripe recommends Metronome for most new usage-based integrations, expressly including usage pricing added to existing flat-rate subscriptions (new lines 9-17). The current source summary (lines 11-21) presents only three ingestion routes and omits this selection boundary, so it would give a misleading entry point for a new integration.

The new comparison distinguishes Stripe /v1/billing/meter_events from Metronome's own ingest API, real-time pricing processing, and continuous balance/usage visibility (new lines 11-13). This is captured documentation guidance, not proof of account-specific availability, measured throughput, or migration obligation.

Existing meter prerequisites, separate legacy documentation, asynchronous summaries/invoices, and API, Dashboard CSV, and Amazon S3 navigation remain in the new capture (old lines 8-20; new lines 19-31). The new See also pricing-models link (new lines 33-35) is navigation only.

The content.diff line 24 has an apparent concatenated duplicate Amazon S3 line; the fully read new raw has one intact Amazon S3 entry at line 31. Treat the raw, rather than that diff artifact, as the page content.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/recording-usage, the November capture adds a substantive Metronome selection recommendation to [[source-stripe-usage-based-billing-recording-usage]]: use Billing Meters here for existing users and consider Metronome for new integrations, including flat-rate subscriptions gaining usage pricing (new lines 11-17).
